source.excerpt: Don’t call me a saint. I don’t want to be dismissed so easily
trail: Robert Ellsberg recalls Day saying this in a lecture preserved by the Catholic Worker. That is a named recollection with institutional provenance, rather than an unsourced inspirational card. Source and attribution evidence ↗

Ellsberg explains her objection to being treated as an exceptional saint whose example ordinary people could dismiss. The source is his recollection, not a dated recording of Day uttering the sentence. Read the supporting source ↗

author.name: Dorothy Day
author.heading: About Dorothy Day
author.bio: Dorothy Day’s words and example are the subject of Robert Ellsberg’s centenary lecture. His recollection connects her resistance to being called a saint with her insistence that ordinary people could follow demanding moral examples.
